claim: Severe dengue infections are characterized by endothelial dysfunction shown to be associated with the secreted nonstructural protein 1 (sNS1).
source: Severe dengue infections are characterized by endothelial dysfunction shown to be associated with the secreted nonstructural protein 1 (sNS1), making it an attractive vaccine antigen and biotherapeutic target.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about dengue pathogenesis.

claim: The major species of isNS1 is a complex of the NS1 dimer partially embedded in a high-density lipoprotein (HDL) particle.
source: Indeed, we found that the major species of isNS1 is a complex of the NS1 dimer partially embedded in a high-density lipoprotein (HDL) particle.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on cryoEM structural determination and biochemical analysis.

claim: Crosslinking mass spectrometry studies confirmed that the isNS1 interacts with the major HDL component ApoA1 through interactions that map to the NS1 wing and hydrophobic domains.
source: Crosslinking mass spectrometry studies confirmed that the isNS1 interacts with the major HDL component ApoA1 through interactions that map to the NS1 wing and hydrophobic domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental crosslinking mass spectrometry data presented in the study.

claim: The sNS1 in sera from DENV-infected mice and a human patient form a similar complex as isNS1.
source: Furthermore, our studies demonstrated that the sNS1 in sera from DENV-infected mice and a human patient form a similar complex as isNS1.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot analysis of mouse and human sera.

claim: DENV is a member of the flavivirus genus and is the cause of significant healthcare problems and economic burden worldwide.
source: Dengue virus (DENV) is a member of the flavivirus genus and is the cause of significant healthcare problems and economic burden worldwide, partially due to the lack of effective therapeutics and the limited efficacy of licensed vaccines, Dengvaxia and QDENGA (Bhatt et al., 2013; Diamond and Pierson, 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The severity of dengue infections has been demonstrated to be correlated to high sera levels of sNS1 in clinical studies.
source: The severity of dengue infections has been demonstrated to be correlated to high sera levels of sNS1 in clinical studies (Libraty et al., 2002; Paranavitane et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical studies.

claim: NS1 exists as intracellular membrane-associated NS1, a presumed GPI-anchored outer plasma membrane-associated NS1, and secreted NS1 (sNS1) during viral infection.
source: The viral nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) is a highly conserved and multifunctional protein that exists as intracellular membrane-associated NS1, a presumed GPI-anchored outer plasma membrane-associated NS1, and secreted NS1 (sNS1) during viral infection (Glasner et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about NS1 protein forms, supported by citation.

claim: Intracellular NS1 found in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lumen is an essential part of the membranous viral RNA replication compartment.
source: Intracellular NS1 found in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) lumen is an essential part of the membranous viral RNA replication compartment (Scaturro et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: sNS1 can induce vascular permeability independently or by inducing pro-inflammatory responses.
source: Upon release from the cells, sNS1 enters the blood circulation where in vitro and in vivo mouse evidence demonstrated its ability to induce vascular permeability, a hallmark of severe dengue, either independently (Puerta-Guardo et al., 2016) or by inducing pro-inflammatory responses (Beatty et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous in vitro and in vivo studies.

claim: High-resolution crystal structures of NS1 dimer have been reported for DENV, West Nile Virus (WNV), and Zika Virus (ZIKV).
source: The high-resolution crystal structures of NS1 dimer have been reported for DENV (Akey et al., 2014), West Nile Virus (WNV) (Akey et al., 2014), and Zika Virus (ZIKV) (Xu et al., 2016; Brown et al., 2016), which provide a conserved molecular view of flaviviral NS1.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: Mature NS1 is 352 amino acids long with an apparent molecular mass between 40 and 50 kDa depending on its glycosylation state.
source: Mature NS1 is 352 amino acids long with an apparent molecular mass between 40 and 50 kDa depending on its glycosylation state.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NS1 protein characteristics.

claim: NS1 has a three-domain architecture: a hydrophobic β-roll (residues 1–29), an α/β wing (38–151), and a β-ladder (181–352).
source: NS1 has a three-domain architecture, a hydrophobic β-roll (residues 1–29), an α/β wing (38–151), and a β-ladder (181–352).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about NS1 protein domains.

claim: sNS1 was reported to be a barrel-shaped hexamer with lipid cargo held together by hydrophobic interactions based on biophysical and low-resolution EM analysis.
source: sNS1 was reported to be a barrel-shaped hexamer with lipid cargo held together by hydrophobic interactions based on biophysical and low-resolution EM analysis (Flamand et al., 1999; Gutsche et al., 2011; Muller et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: Recent cryoEM structures of recombinant sNS1 (rsNS1) from DENV-2 showed mainly tetrameric rsNS1, with only 3% of the population found to be in the hexameric form.
source: Recent cryoEM structures of recombinant sNS1 (rsNS1) from DENV-2 showed mainly tetrameric rsNS1, with only 3% of the population found to be in the hexameric form Shu et al., 2022.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a recent cryoEM study.

claim: The lipid profile of DENV-1 infection-derived sNS1 is similar to high-density lipoprotein (HDL).
source: While earlier studies by Gutsche et al, (2011) found that the lipid profile of DENV-1 infection-derived sNS1 to be similar to high-density lipoprotein (HDL) Gutsche et al., 2011, the same research group now showed that DENV-2 rsNS1 could dock onto HDL with direct visualization using negative stain EM analysis as reported by Benfrid et al., 2022.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: DENV-2 rsNS1 could dock onto HDL with direct visualization using negative stain EM analysis.
source: While earlier studies by Gutsche et al, (2011) found that the lipid profile of DENV-1 infection-derived sNS1 to be similar to high-density lipoprotein (HDL) Gutsche et al., 2011, the same research group now showed that DENV-2 rsNS1 could dock onto HDL with direct visualization using negative stain EM analysis as reported by Benfrid et al., 2022.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: sNS1 appears to utilize the scavenger receptor B1, a known receptor for HDL, as the cognate receptor in cultured cells.
source: Additionally, sNS1 appears to utilize the scavenger receptor B1, a known receptor for HDL, as the cognate receptor in cultured cells (Alcalá et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: The T164S mutation in the greasy finger loop between the wing and β-ladder interdomain of NS1 was identified from a DENV2 epidemic in Cuba in 1997, where a correlation with enhanced clinical disease severity was observed.
source: The T164S mutation in the greasy finger loop between the wing and β-ladder interdomain of NS1 was identified from a DENV2 epidemic in Cuba in 1997, where a correlation with enhanced clinical disease severity was observed (Rodriguez-Roche et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to epidemiological research.

claim: The T164S mutation in NS1 could directly cause lethality in mice and increased sNS1 secretion.
source: We demonstrated that this single mutation in NS1 could directly cause lethality in mice and increased sNS1 secretion (Chan et al., 2019), which served as an epidemiologically relevant tool to study the biochemical and structural characteristics of sNS1 in this study.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: The isNS1 is a complex of the NS1 dimer embedded on a single HDL particle composed of ApoA1.
source: We determined that the isNS1 is a complex of the NS1 dimer embedded on a single HDL particle composed of ApoA1.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on integrative structural approaches.

claim: Both immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt and isNS1ts retained a molecular size of ~250 kDa as detected with Coomassie blue and on a western blot using Ab56.2 following separation on a Native-PAGE.
source: Both immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt and isNS1ts retained a molecular size of ~250 kDa as detected with Coomassie blue and on a western blot using Ab56.2 following separation on a Native-PAGE (Figure 1b, Figure 1—source data 1 and 2, Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3, Figure 1—figure supplement 2—source data 1–3), as previously reported (Chan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b and supplementary figures, as well as citation to previous work.

claim: The isNS1wt migrated slower than the rsNS1 protein, indicating possible conformational or oligomeric differences between the two NS1 species.
source: The isNS1wt migrated slower than the rsNS1 protein (a gift from Shu et al., 2022), indicating possible conformational or oligomeric differences between the two NS1 species (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: On a reducing SDS-PAGE, two major bands of approximately 50 kDa and 25 kDa were identified in isNS1wt, the former corresponding to the single monomeric NS1 band seen in rsNS1.
source: On a reducing SDS-PAGE, we identified two major bands of approximately 50 kDa and 25 kDa in isNS1wt, the former corresponding to the single monomeric NS1 band seen in rsNS1 (Figure 1c, Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Preliminary mass ID identified the 25 kDa protein as bovine apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), a major component of HDL in bovine serum-containing culture media, which has a reported molecular weight of 28 kDa.
source: Preliminary mass ID identified the 25 kDa protein as bovine apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), a major component of HDL in bovine serum-containing culture media, which has a reported molecular weight of 28 kDa (Kitti, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and citation.

claim: The combined LFQ intensity of NS1 and ApoA1 accounted for more than 77.6 and 88.6% of the total ion intensity count (TIC) detected from the elute fraction and the 250 kDa band, respectively.
source: We found that the combined LFQ intensity of NS1 and ApoA1 accounted for more than 77.6 and 88.6% of the total ion intensity count (TIC) detected from the elute fraction (Figure 1a, blue box) and the 250 kDa band (Figure 1b, the purple box labeled '1'), respectively, indicating that NS1 and ApoA1 were the major proteins in the elute fraction and the ~250 kDa band from immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by label-free quantification LC-MS data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: NS1 accounted for 96.85% of the TIC for the 50 kDa band.
source: Accordingly, as depicted in Figure 1d, NS1 accounted for 96.85% of the TIC for the 50 kDa band (Figure 1c, red box '2'), while the intensity of ApoA1 accounted for 96.23% of the TIC for the 25 kDa band (Figure 1c, green box '3').
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: ApoA1 accounted for 96.23% of the TIC for the 25 kDa band.
source: Accordingly, as depicted in Figure 1d, NS1 accounted for 96.85% of the TIC for the 50 kDa band (Figure 1c, red box '2'), while the intensity of ApoA1 accounted for 96.23% of the TIC for the 25 kDa band (Figure 1c, green box '3').
evidence: This claim is supported by LC-MS data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The 3D reconstruction of isNS1ts alone was observed to have no discernible features beyond a spherical-like density with varying dimensions averaging around 106 Å by 77 Å.
source: However, the 3D reconstruction of isNS1ts alone was observed to have no discernible features beyond a spherical-like density with varying dimensions averaging around 106 Å by 77 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 4b and c).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Both isNS1wt:Ab56.2 and isNS1wt:Fab56.2 samples resulted in similarly distinguishable 2D class averages which show asymmetrical binding of one unit of Fab56.2 to the dimeric cross-shaped sNS1 associated with a lower-density sphere, presumably HDL.
source: Overall, both samples resulted in similarly distinguishable 2D class averages (Figure 2b and c), which show asymmetrical binding of one unit of Fab56.2 to the dimeric cross-shaped sNS1 associated with a lower-density sphere, presumably HDL.
evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM 2D class averages shown in Figure 2b and c.

claim: In the isNS1wt:Fab56.2 ternary complex dataset, two apparent but rare sub-classes of free sNS1wt dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 representing 3.5% of the total population of picked particles were observed.
source: In the isNS1wt:Fab56.2 ternary complex dataset, we further observed two apparent but rare sub-classes of free sNS1wt dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 representing 3.5% of the total population of picked particles (Figure 2c, red dashed boxes).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The AlphaFold2 predicted model of the NS1 dimer and Fab models fitted into the cryoEM map with a correlation value of 0.75 to the fitted regions using a simulated 5 Å map.
source: While the cryoEM map reconstructions remain limited at low resolutions (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), they could be fitted with the NS1 dimer and Fab56.2 models (Figure 2d) predicted separately using AlphaFold2 (Jumper et al., 2021; Mirdita et al., 2022), with a correlation value of 0.75 to the fitted regions using a simulated 5 Å map from the NS1 dimer and Fab models.
evidence: This claim is supported by model fitting to cryoEM data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The approximate dimensions of the spherical HDL could be measured at 82 Å by 65 Å.
source: The approximate dimensions of the spherical HDL could also be measured at 82 Å by 65 Å (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), which aligned with existing reports of spherical HDL being measured at 70–120 Å in diameter with predominantly homodimeric ApoA1 arranged as an anti-parallel double-belt stabilized by intermolecular salt bridges (Silva et al., 2008; He et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM measurements shown in supplementary figures and citations to previous HDL structural studies.

claim: The NS1 dimer appears semi-embedded on the HDL particle through its hydrophobic surface, with a conformation that exposed only one end of the β-ladder domain to which Ab56.2 and Fab56.2 bind.
source: The NS1 dimer appears semi-embedded on the HDL particle through its hydrophobic surface, with a conformation that exposed only one end of the β-ladder domain to which Ab56.2 and Fab56.2 bind.
evidence: This claim is based on interpretation of the cryoEM structural model.

claim: 2D class averages of isNS1ts:Fab56.2 dataset showed a significant sub-population of a free NS1ts dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 (53.7%), in addition to the HDL spheres (23.6%) and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 (22.7%) classes.
source: Interestingly, 2D class averages of isNS1ts:Fab56.2 dataset showed a significant sub-population of a free NS1ts dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 (53.7%), in addition to the HDL spheres (23.6%) and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 (22.7%) classes (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM 2D classification data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: A comparison of the cryoEM density maps of free isNS1ts dimer:Fab56.2 and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 ternary complex revealed a pose difference of the Fab56.2 between the free isNS1ts dimer and the HDL-bound isNS1ts dimer.
source: A comparison of the cryoEM density maps of free isNS1ts dimer:Fab56.2 (Figure 3D, gray) and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 ternary complex (Figure 3d, yellow) fitted with a correlation value of 0.71 based on the NS1 map region revealed a pose difference of the Fab56.2 between the free isNS1ts dimer and the HDL-bound isNS1ts dimer (Figure 3d, inset).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of cryoEM maps shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Comparison of the density maps of the isNS1 dimer:HDL population in the Fab56.2 ternary complexes of isNS1wt and isNS1ts revealed conformational similarities of the isNS1 dimer:HDL complex.
source: Further comparison of the density maps of the isNS1 dimer:HDL population in the Fab56.2 ternary complexes of isNS1wt (Figure 3e, purple) and isNS1ts (Figure 3e, yellow) revealed conformational similarities of the isNS1 dimer:HDL complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of cryoEM maps shown in Figure 3e.

claim: 28 NS1:NS1 and 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, as well as 25 NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks were identified for isNS1wt.
source: We identified 28 NS1:NS1 and 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, as well as 25 NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for isNS1wt (Figure 4b; Supplementary file 2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and supplementary files.

claim: The NS1 residues that are involved in both intra- and intermolecular crosslinks were located mainly on the β-roll and wing domains, with ~34% of the NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks being located on the β-roll domain.
source: As depicted in Figure 4b and c, the NS1 residues that are involved in both intra- and intermolecular crosslinks were located mainly on the β-roll and wing domains, with ~34% of the NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks being located on the β-roll domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and c.

claim: 85% of the NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks (24 out of 28) met the 30 Å cutoff distance criterion for the Cα atoms of crosslinked residues on the predicted NS1 dimer model.
source: The NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslink pairs were further validated on the predicted NS1 dimer model by implementing a 30 Å cutoff distance for the Cα atoms of crosslinked residues, a criterion that was met by 85% of the NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks (24 out of 28; Figure 4d).
evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the structural model shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for the immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt were found to be located between the β-roll and wing domains of NS1 and the helices 3, 4, 8, and 10 of ApoA1.
source: The NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for the immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt were found to be located between the β-roll and wing domains of NS1 and the helices 3, 4, 8, and 10 of ApoA1 (Figure 4b and d).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and d.

claim: 76% of the NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks (19 out of 25) satisfied the <30 Å distance between their Cα atoms cutoff when validated on the cryoEM model of isNS1wt.
source: Applying the same cutoff value of <30 Å distance between the Cα atoms of the NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinked residues and validating it on the cryoEM model of isNS1wt in this study (Figure 4d and e) satisfied 76% of the crosslinks (19 out of 25 intermolecular crosslinks between NS1 dimer and ApoA1).
evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the cryoEM model shown in Figure 4d and e.

claim: 62% of the ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks (18 out of 29) satisfied the <30 Å distance between their Cα atoms cutoff.
source: In the case of ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, the <30 Å distance between their Cα atoms cutoff satisfied 62% of the crosslinks (18 out of 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks).
evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the structural model.

claim: The higher number of violated crosslinks in ApoA1:ApoA1 compared to those in NS1:NS1 could be due to the flexible and dynamic nature of ApoA1 dimers.
source: The higher number of violated crosslinks in ApoA1:ApoA1 compared to those in NS1:NS1 could be due to the flexible and dynamic nature of ApoA1 dimers, which may prevent it from assuming a fixed relative position among the ApoA1 dimer population in the HDL.
evidence: This is an interpretation/speculation based on the crosslinking data and known properties of ApoA1.

claim: isNS1ts dimer may have a weaker affinity to HDL in comparison to the isNS1wt dimer.
source: This indicated that isNS1ts dimer may have a weaker affinity to HDL in comparison to the isNS1wt dimer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of fewer crosslink sites in isNS1ts and the presence of free isNS1ts dimers in cryoEM data.

claim: The crosslinked rsNS1 alone appeared as higher oligomer bands of dimers, tetramers, and hexamers on the SDS-PAGE analysis.
source: The crosslinked rsNS1 alone appeared as higher oligomer bands of dimers, tetramers, and hexamers on the SDS-PAGE analysis (Figure 4f, lane 3, Figure 4—source data 2), which differed from the crosslinked isNS1 (Figure 4a, lane 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by SDS-PAGE data shown in Figure 4f.

claim: The addition of human HDL and crosslinker to rsNS1 resulted in a smearing band ranging from 30 to 150 kDa with the loss of the well-defined monomeric rsNS1 band.
source: Interestingly, the addition of human HDL and crosslinker resulted in a smearing band ranging from 30 to 150 kDa with the loss of the well-defined monomeric rsNS1 band (Figure 4f, lane 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by SDS-PAGE data shown in Figure 4f.

claim: In the crosslinked rsNS1 in the absence of HDL, 17 NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks at the β-roll and wing domains were identified.
source: In the crosslinked rsNS1 in the absence of HDL, we identified 17 NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks at the β-roll and wing domains (Figure 4f and g, Supplementary file 4 and 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4f and g.

claim: In the presence of human HDL, 30 ApoA1:ApoA1, 4 NS1:NS1, and 6 NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks were identified in rsNS1 samples.
source: In the presence of human HDL, we identified 30 ApoA1:ApoA1, 4 NS1:NS1, and 6 NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks (Supplementary file 4 and 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data in supplementary files.

claim: Only one out of six rsNS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks was within the 30 Å cutoff distance when mapped to the NS1:ApoA1 cryoEM model.
source: Only one out of six rsNS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks was within the 30 Å cutoff distance when mapped to the NS1:ApoA1 cryoEM model (Figure 4e).
evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the cryoEM model.

claim: rsNS1 may form oligomers of dimers but not a complex with HDL under the tested conditions.
source: Overall, this suggests that rsNS1 may form oligomers of dimers but not a complex with HDL under the tested conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the crosslinking mass spectrometry data comparing rsNS1 with and without HDL.

claim: The greatest competition in the NS1 peptide competition ELISA was observed at the NS1 peptide spanning residues 316–330 out of 301–340.
source: The greatest competition was observed at the NS1 peptide spanning residues 316–330 out of 301–340 which showed a decrease in OD450 absorbance (Figure 5b).
evidence: This claim is supported by peptide competition ELISA data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Comparative HDX results revealed global-scale protection against deuterium exchange of rsNS1c in the presence of Fab56.2.
source: Comparative HDX results revealed global-scale protection against deuterium exchange of rsNS1c in the presence of Fab56.2 (Figure 6a, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a), indicative of reduced conformational dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Large-scale differences in deuterium exchange were primarily observed across peptides spanning the dimer interface (residues 174–186) and at the tip of the C-terminal β-ladder (residues 286–347) of rsNS1c.
source: Large-scale differences in deuterium exchange were primarily observed across peptides spanning the dimer interface (residues 174–186) and at the tip of the C-terminal β-ladder (residues 286–347) of rsNS1c (Figure 6b).
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Multiple overlapping peptides, spanning residues 286–347, showed protection against deuterium exchange even at the longer labeling times (100 min) in rsNS1c:Fab56.2 complex.
source: Multiple overlapping peptides, spanning residues 286–347 (Figure 6b), showed protection against deuterium exchange even at the longer labeling times (100 min) in rsNS1c:Fab56.2 complex (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6b and supplementary data.

claim: rsNS1c binds stably to Fab56.2 at the primary epitope site of residues 300–310.
source: Coupled with the observation that the most significant change in the differential plot was at residues 300–310 (Figure 6a), these results collectively indicate that rsNS1c binds stably to Fab56.2 at the primary epitope site of residues 300–310.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6a and other supporting data.

claim: Comparative HDX results of rsNS1c-bound and free Fab56.2 revealed protection against deuterium exchange of all three complementarity-determining regions (CDR) of the heavy chain and CDRL2 of the light chain.
source: Comparative HDX results of rsNS1c-bound and free Fab56.2 revealed protection against deuterium exchange of all three complementarity-determining regions (CDR) of the heavy chain (Figure 6c, Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) and CDRL2 of the light chain (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6c and d.

claim: Peptides spanning CDRH3 (residues 89–116) showed the largest magnitude decrease in deuterium exchange at all labeling time points upon binding to rsNS1c.
source: Upon binding to rsNS1c, peptides spanning CDRH3 (residues 89–116) showed the largest magnitude decrease in deuterium exchange at all labeling time points, while CDRH2 showed minor significant differences.
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data.

claim: Only the CDRL2 loop (residues 49–56) of the light chain of Fab56.2 showed significantly decreased deuterium exchange upon binding to rsNS1c.
source: In addition, only the CDRL2 loop (residues 49–56) of the light chain of Fab56.2 showed significantly decreased deuterium exchange.
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data.

claim: CDRH1-3 and CDRL2 loops were spatially co-localized to form the paratope site to bind rsNS1c, with the heavy chain being the primary anchor.
source: Mapping of the deuterium exchange profiles of heavy and light chains onto a model of Fab56.2 (Figure 6e) revealed that CDRH1-3 and CDRL2 loops were spatially co-localized to form the paratope site to bind rsNS1c, with the heavy chain being the primary anchor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on HDX-MS data mapped onto the Fab56.2 model shown in Figure 6e.

claim: The mouse sera immunoaffinity purified sNS1ts was detected at ~250 kDa by both anti-ApoA1 and anti-NS1 antibodies in a western blot analysis following separation on a Native-PAGE.
source: The mouse sera immunoaffinity purified sNS1ts was detected at ~250 kDa by both anti-ApoA1 and anti-NS1 antibodies in a western blot analysis following separation on a Native-PAGE (Figure 7a, Figure 7—source data 1), supporting our mass spectrometry finding that ApoA1 is part of the ~250 kDa isNS1 protein complex purified from infected Vero cells (Figure 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from mouse sera shown in Figure 7a.

claim: Increasing the anti-ApoA1 antibody from 10 to 50 µg coupled onto Protein AG resin for pull-down resulted in a corresponding increase in the sNS1 amount detected by ELISA in human patient serum.
source: Increasing the anti-ApoA1 antibody from 10 to 50 µg coupled onto Protein AG resin for pull-down resulted in a corresponding increase in the sNS1 amount detected by ELISA (Figure 7b), suggesting a specific association between sNS1 and ApoA1.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and ELISA data from human patient serum shown in Figure 7b.

claim: NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1.
source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence similarity data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and citation to structural conservation.

claim: Bovine HDL has approximately 79% sequence similarity to human HDL.
source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mouse HDL has approximately 65% sequence similarity to human HDL.
source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved.
source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The data points to the association of ApoA1 with sNS1 in vivo.
source: Collectively, despite the limited amount of sNS1 in sera samples from DENV-infected mice or humans, our data points to the association of ApoA1 with sNS1 in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from mouse and human sera.

claim: Benfrid et al. (2022) reconstituted complexes of rsNS1 dimers bound to the surface of a spheroid human HDL particle in vitro at 1:1 to 3:1 ratio when up to 400 μg/mL of rsNS1 were used.
source: Benfrid et al. (2022) recently reconstituted complexes of rsNS1 dimers bound to the surface of a spheroid human HDL particle in vitro at 1:1 to 3:1 ratio when up to 400 μg/mL of rsNS1 were used Benfrid et al., 2022.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research.

claim: Up to two NS1 dimers docked onto an HDL particle were observed in studies with infection-derived sNS1 (isNS1).
source: Similarly, in our studies with infection-derived sNS1 (isNS1), we observed up to two NS1 dimers docked onto an HDL particle (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c, Figures 2 and 3, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The concentration of isNS1:HDL in the study (~30 μg/mL) is closer to the maximum clinically reported concentration of sNS1 in the sera of DENV patients (50 μg/mL).
source: It is noteworthy that the concentration of isNS1:HDL in our study (~30 μg/mL) is closer to the maximum clinically reported concentration of sNS1 in the sera of DENV patients (50 μg/mL) Libraty et al., 2002; Young et al., 2000; Alcon et al., 2002.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with clinically reported concentrations cited from previous studies.

claim: The ratio of sNS1 to HDL varies depending on the concentration of the proteins used for complex formation.
source: Therefore, the ratio of sNS1 to HDL varies depending on the concentration of the proteins used for complex formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of different experimental conditions.

claim: The data does not support the widely held view that sNS1 is composed of a trimer of NS1 dimers with an ~28 Å wide central channel filled with lipid.
source: While our study is limited to only one antibody (56.2) for immunoaffinity purification, our key take-home message in terms of structure is that our data does not support the widely held view that sNS1 is composed of a trimer of NS1 dimers with an ~28 Å wide central channel filled with lipid as established in several seminal publications (Flamand et al., 1999; Gutsche et al., 2011; Muller et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural data from this study compared to previous models.

claim: The data confirms the observations reported in Benfrid et al., 2022.
source: In fact, our data confirms the observations reported in Benfrid et al., 2022.
evidence: This is a statement comparing the current findings with previous research.

claim: In the rare instances where trimer of dimers have been experimentally shown by cryoEM of rNS1 structures, only a single lipid molecule can be found in the narrow central channel.
source: In the rare instances where trimer of dimers have been experimentally shown by cryoEM of rNS1 structures (Shu et al., 2022), only a single lipid molecule can be found in the narrow central channel and unlikely to be reflective of sNS1 circulating in serum.
evidence: This claim is based on citation to previous cryoEM studies and interpretation of their findings.

claim: The amount of lipid associated with infection-derived sNS1 is consistent with NS1 dimer(s) associated with HDL.
source: We argue that the amount of lipid associated with infection-derived sNS1 (Gutsche et al., 2011; Chan et al., 2019) is consistent with NS1 dimer(s) associated with HDL.
evidence: This is an argument based on comparison of lipid content data from previous studies with the current structural model.

claim: The interaction with HDL requires an exposed hydrophobic face of NS1 that is incompatible to the hexamer model of sNS1.
source: The interaction with HDL requires an exposed hydrophobic face of NS1 that is incompatible to the hexamer model of sNS1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural requirements for NS1-HDL interaction.

claim: The oligomeric state of NS1 is dynamic, which may vary depending on the context and environment.
source: Indeed, it is agreeable that the oligomeric state of NS1 is dynamic, which may vary depending on the context and environment.
evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging the complexity of NS1 oligomerization.

claim: Incubating immunoaffinity-purified sNS1 with human PBMCs from three independent human donors triggered the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNFα in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: Our previous functional studies comparing isNS1wt with isNS1ts (T164S) showed that incubating immunoaffinity-purified sNS1 with human PBMCs from three independent human donors triggered the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNFα in a concentration-dependent manner and that it was more pronounced with the mutant than the WT (Chan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous functional studies by the authors.

claim: The proinflammatory cytokine production was more pronounced with the isNS1ts mutant than the WT.
source: Our previous functional studies comparing isNS1wt with isNS1ts (T164S) showed that incubating immunoaffinity-purified sNS1 with human PBMCs from three independent human donors triggered the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNFα in a concentration-dependent manner and that it was more pronounced with the mutant than the WT (Chan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous functional studies by the authors.

claim: Acid-eluted isNS1 proteins in this study induce endothelial hyperpermeability.
source: Furthermore, we have provisional transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER) assay data with isNS1 proteins used in the structural studies with human umbilical vascular endothelial cells (hUVEC), which show that acid-eluted isNS1 proteins in this study induces endothelial hyperpermeability as shown in previous studies (Puerta-Guardo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is based on provisional TEER assay data and citation to previous studies.

claim: The presence of a significant population of free isNS1ts dimers in complex with Fab56.2 and fewer crosslinks identified between isNS1ts and ApoA1 point toward the possibility that isNS1ts is more dynamic in its association with host proteins than isNS1wt.
source: The presence of a significant population of free isNS1ts dimers in complex with Fab56.2 and fewer crosslinks identified between isNS1ts and ApoA1 point toward the possibility that isNS1ts is more dynamic in its association with host proteins than isNS1wt.
evidence: This is an inference based on cryoEM and crosslinking data comparing isNS1wt and isNS1ts.

claim: The disease severity and increased complement protein expression in AG129 mice liver infected with NS1T164S carrying virus compared with WT can be ascribed to weakly bound mutant NS1 with fast on/off rate with HDL being transported to the liver where specific receptors bind to free sNS1 and interact with effector proteins such as complement to drive inflammation and associated pathology.
source: The disease severity and increased complement protein expression in AG129 mice liver infected with NS1T164S carrying virus compared with WT that was observed in our previous study (Chan et al., 2019) can be ascribed to weakly bound mutant NS1 with fast on/off rate with HDL being transported to the liver where specific receptors bind to free sNS1 and interact with effector proteins such as complement to drive inflammation and associated pathology.
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation based on previous in vivo data and the current structural findings.

claim: Contrary to the known protective roles of HDL, sNS1:HDL complex triggers proinflammatory signals when tested with primary human macrophages.
source: Contrary to the known protective roles of HDL such as against endotoxic shock caused by lipopolysaccharides (Trinder et al., 2020; Tall, 2021; Harsløf et al., 2023), Benfrid et al. (2022) showed that sNS1:HDL complex triggers proinflammatory signals when tested with primary human macrophages (Benfrid et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on HDL protective roles and sNS1:HDL complex effects.

claim: The presence of sNS1:HDL complexes as a predominant population of sNS1 in the in vitro infection model corroborates with a previous report of an interaction between insect-derived recombinant NS1 and the classical HDL/ApoA1-binding receptor known as SR-BI.
source: The presence of sNS1:HDL complexes as a predominant population of sNS1 in our in vitro infection model corroborates with a previous report of an interaction between insect-derived recombinant NS1 and the classical HDL/ApoA1-binding receptor known as SR-BI (Alcalá et al., 2022), which is primarily expressed on hepatocytes (Acton et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim connects the current findings with previous research through citations.

claim: SR-BI is primarily expressed on hepatocytes.
source: The presence of sNS1:HDL complexes as a predominant population of sNS1 in our in vitro infection model corroborates with a previous report of an interaction between insect-derived recombinant NS1 and the classical HDL/ApoA1-binding receptor known as SR-BI (Alcalá et al., 2022), which is primarily expressed on hepatocytes (Acton et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The interaction with SR-BI in hepatocytes has been suggested to trigger endocytosis of sNS1 and subsequent downstream effects including vascular permeability.
source: This interaction in hepatocytes has been suggested to trigger endocytosis of sNS1 and subsequent downstream effects including vascular permeability, which is a characteristic feature of severe dengue (Alcalá et al., 2022; Alcon-LePoder et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Internalization of sNS1 is critical for increased virus production in hepatocytes.
source: Internalization of sNS1 is critical for increased virus production in hepatocytes (Alcon-LePoder et al., 2005) and NS1-mediated permeability in endothelial cells (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Internalization of sNS1 is critical for NS1-mediated permeability in endothelial cells.
source: Internalization of sNS1 is critical for increased virus production in hepatocytes (Alcon-LePoder et al., 2005) and NS1-mediated permeability in endothelial cells (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: NS1:HDL complexes have been shown to induce the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines in macrophages.
source: Furthermore, NS1:HDL complexes have been shown to induce the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines in macrophages and their presence has been detected in the sera of hospitalized DENV patients Benfrid et al., 2022.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: NS1:HDL complexes have been detected in the sera of hospitalized DENV patients.
source: Furthermore, NS1:HDL complexes have been shown to induce the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines in macrophages and their presence has been detected in the sera of hospitalized DENV patients Benfrid et al., 2022.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: rsNS1 has been shown to trigger a TLR4-mediated release of proinflammatory cytokines to induce vascular leakage.

(2021) further showed that lipid-free recombinant ApoA1 neutralizes the proinflammatory effects caused by insect-derived recombinant intracellular NS1 (Coelho et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

source: While rsNS1 has been shown to trigger a TLR4-mediated release of proinflammatory cytokines to induce vascular leakage (Modhiran et al., 2015; Coelho et al., 2021), Coelho et al. (2021) further showed that lipid-free recombinant ApoA1 neutralizes the proinflammatory effects caused by insect-derived recombinant intracellular NS1 (Coelho et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.
